messages.subject: Re: problems with frotify
parts:
You can run R out of a folder on your desktop. I do it every day on my work machine. I cannot install anything. If you're on Windows (likely) you can use the --internet2 flag for R to use Internet Exploder's proxy settings and use that to download packages. 

In other words, my suggestion would be to try and run a newer version of R and ggplot2. 2.13 and 0.89 are both fairly old at this point. 

If you really really can't install R in a folder and run it that way, could you post a reproducible example?

On Wed, Aug 29, 2012 at 2:53 AM, gylamb <gyl...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi guys,
 
I got inspried by the nice maps on website and I want to do something similar use ggplot2 but I got some problems.
My R version is 2.13.0 and ggplot2 is 0.8.9. I am working in a government agency so I couldn't update them to
the latest version easily.
 
First, I load shapefile to R,
 TAmap = readShapePoly(shapefile_ta,IDvar="TA06")
> class(TAmap)
[1] "SpatialPolygonsDataFrame"
attr(,"package")
[1] "sp"
 
Then, I want to fortify TAmap to a dataframe which can be used in ggplot2.
I tried fortify.sp and fortify.map and shown that
 
 > TAmap2 = fortify.sp(TAmap,region="TA06")
Error: could not find function "fortify.sp"
I think it because my ggplot2 version is old.
 
I also tried
fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame
TAmap2=fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(TAmap,region="TA06")
I got my R crashed if I run this code.
 
If I plot map without fortify, R crashed as well.
 
Could any help me with that problem please? All I want to do is to draw some nice maps.
 
Thanks in advance,
Yang
